author: HiddenGap
text:
I believe we can call the modifications set.

The new modifications are: A. There must be a WRB in the sequence. This isn't so much a new rule as it is making the appearance of a WRB definitive.

B. The initial Start Point (SP) must appear 1-

intervals after the WRB. We've gone

from 1-3 to 1-4. Therefore, there can be 3 intervals after the WRB before we see the SP.

C. The Long Lower Shadow (for longs) of the initial Start Point (SP) must be greater than the lower shadows of all the intervals after the WRB and the 3 intervals prior to the WRB. And the Long Lower Shadow must be larger than the bodies of said intervals as well. But the Long Lower Shadow does not have to be larger than the combination of the lower shadow and the body of any interval except its own.

Great questions, keep them coming. I will start with this one first.

One of our goals is to create an entry signal that is specific and rule-based, yet broad enough to cover a myriad of situations. To that end, we have not mentioned any type of color (close vs open) requirements for any of the intervals. I have noticed that the majority (almost all) of the valid short signals will have a White (close>open) WRB. And the valid long signals will have Dark (close<open) WRB. But again, that is not a requirement, only an observation.

Along those same lines, we have not made any such requirement for any of the intervals involved in the pattern. For example, we have NOT said that there must be a Dark (close>open) interval within the 3 intervals prior to the WRB

Once again, great question. I appreciate your participation.

The WRB closest to the SP would be skipped. By definition, the closest WRB in this situation would be the largest. So we would look for the Upper/Lower Shadow of the SP to be larger than the bodies of the 3 intervals prior to the closest WRB

hieronymus wrote: Ok cool, so we do have a stop run / confirmation candle in one now as well, I like that! So if SP is also the CC then it just has to close above body of previous candle right?

No. The CC has two rules: (1) the CC must close above the body of the previous candle. (2) the body of the CC must be larger than the body of the previous candle.

So our SP & CC combo must meet both rules of the CC and all the rules of the SP.

You continue to ask stellar questions. One thing I have avoided discussing is the idea of a "contingency" plan. What I mean by "contingency" plan is price action that would not only tell us we are wrong, but would also suggest we take a trade in the opposite direction. I do not like "contingency" plan set-ups, because they would have us going long in Supply Zones and short in Demand Zones. However, we may still want to focus on a particular Price Action piece typically found in a "contingency" plan. The WRB. I will get into the concept on the next post. For now, just realize that we also have a Nullification Candle (NC). The white (open<close) WRB in this picture, although we are not happy to see it, would not be a NC.

One thing I should mention about placing our stops. I have been saying the stop should be roughly 5 pips from the high/low of the SP. I have been using 5 because that is what DTML use. But they are taking the trades on a 15 minute chart. 5 pips may or may not be appropriate on a 1 hour chart. They are also trying to keep the over risk to 20 pips. Again, 20 pips may or may not be appropriate on a 1 hour time frame.

Akif,

While there will always be losing trades, let's take a closer look at these here.

A1: I am not sure that this is in fact a valid SP. The long lower shadow does not look larger than the body of the candle before it. Nor does it look larger than the lower shadow of the candle before it. The Confirmation Entry is a VISUAL ENTRY. That means the better set-ups tend to be those that you can tell meet the requirements visually with ease. Now, you may do the actual math and conclude that lower shadow is larger than the body of the previous candle. But when you can make that determination easily with the naked eye, the set-up tends to be better.

B1: This is more of an obvious valid SP. A valid signal is produced, which results in a loss.

Let's take a closer look at B5. This is a White (open<close) WRB that appears 1-3 intervals after our entry candle and closes higher than the high of the entry candle. That is a Nullification Candle (NC). In this case, the NC stops us out. But if it had not stopped us out, we would want to be exiting, or at the very least, moving our stop closer to our entry price. A true "contingency" plan would have us stop and reverse our position. Especially since the WRB preceded a doji candle line.

The other place where an NC can appear is after the SP but before confirmation. This NC would tell us not to enter the trade at all.

Note that our NC could be the interval that both enters us into the trade during its creation and tells us to exit once it is complete. Which is the case here.

author: HiddenGap
text:
Here's a schematic with a few examples of the NC.

Key points:

1. Any white (open<close) WRB that closes higher than the high of our SP is a NC. If the NC appears before the CC, we would not enter at all.

2. If we are in a short trade, a white (open<close) WRB 1-3 intervals after our entry candle that closes higher than the high of said candle, is a NC.
